newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela looking at alternatives to Brady buyback.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela looking at alternatives to Brady buyback.

text.p: The prospect of a Brady bond buy-back for Venezuela is not as attractive as it was, and the country is now looking at alternatives, Finance Minister Venezuela Luis Raul Matos Azocar said on Wednesday.
"It's still a good opportunity. But not as good as it was when they were at 45 percent," he told reporters during a conference in London.

Venezuela FLIRB Brady bonds are currently fetching more than 91 cents in the dollar. They were around 45 cents at the end of 1995, before the government reached an agreement with the International Monetary Fund for a loan.
"We will have to look for some other approach," Matos said but declined to be spcific.
The government is setting up a debt rescue fund which he said at the moment has $800 million from privatisation.
Proceeds from the sale of aluminium and steel firms will bring another $3 billion, he added.
The fund is to be used to pay off foreign and domestic debt.
